title: docs(architecture): teach the exported DataSource, and the App Router client boundary
body:
Fixes #8160

Fixes #8161

Two defects on one page (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`), collapsed into one PR so the two never race the same file. They are **not** a family fold: the defect forms differ, so each card keeps its own acceptance criterion and its own evidence below. Neither card inherits the other's.

> Notation: quoted TypeScript diagnostics use square brackets where the compiler prints angle brackets (`DataSource[any]` for the generic instantiation). GitHub's body sanitizer eats short tag-shaped fragments, including inside backticks.

## The two truths — what the page taught vs. what the tree exports

| | the page taught (before) | the tree exports (`packages/types/src/data.ts`) |
|---|---|---|
| interface source | a **locally re-declared** `interface DataSource` | `DataSource`, **exported** by `@object-ui/types` |
| required members | 5 (`find`, `findOne`, `create`, `update`, `delete`) | **6** — the same five plus `getObjectSchema` |
| `getMetadata` | declared, optional | **does not exist**: `grep -rn "getMetadata" packages/types/src/` returns nothing |
| `getObjectSchema` | absent | required, and the doc comment on it says so: *"Required for all DataSource implementations to support schema-aware components."* |
| the consuming prop | — | `ObjectViewProps.dataSource: DataSource` (`packages/plugin-view/dist/ObjectView.d.ts:75`) — **required, and the real type** |
| App Router fences | no `'use client'` anywhere on the page | the packages ship no `'use client'` banner either, so the consumer's file is the only place the boundary can be declared |

Required-member census, re-derived rather than quoted:

```
$ sed -n '350,935p' packages/types/src/data.ts | grep -oE '^  [a-zA-Z]+\('
  find(          findOne(       create(
  update(        delete(        getObjectSchema(
```
Six. Every other member of `DataSource` carries `?`.

## Card #8160 — before / after, with the probe

The probe is the gate's own harness: `compileSnippets()` from `scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs`, so the stand-in is judged against the **built** `dist/*.d.ts` exactly as a reader who copies the page would be. The interface text is read off disk, never retyped.

**Before** — a stand-in annotated with the page's verbatim interface, handed to `ObjectView`:

```
--- harness controls ---
resolution -> packages/types/dist/index.d.ts
sentinel   -> TS2305        (a planted missing export is still caught)
positive   -> 0 diagnostic(s)
--- probe result ---
parseFailures: 0  semanticallyJudged: 1
  TS2741: Property 'getObjectSchema' is missing in type 'DataSource' but required in type 'DataSource[any]'.
```

The card's measured diagnostic reproduces exactly. **The card's reading stands.**

**After** — the same probe against what the page now teaches, again read verbatim off disk:

```
--- probe result ---
parseFailures: 0  semanticallyJudged: 1
  ZERO DIAGNOSTICS
```

Route **甲** as dispatched: the page now imports the exported type instead of re-declaring it. Route 乙 was not needed and is not taken — a self-consistent minimal subset **does** exist (the six required members), so no new public contract had to be invented.

What the page now teaches, and why each line is load-bearing rather than decorative:

- `type MinimalDataSource = Pick[DataSource, 'find' | 'findOne' | 'create' | 'update' | 'delete' | 'getObjectSchema']` — names the six, and the *names* are compiler-checked.
- `export const adapter: DataSource = minimal` — proves the six **suffice**. It goes red the moment a seventh member becomes required.

Both halves are checked, not asserted. Negative control on that claim — swapping the page's old `getMetadata` back into the `Pick`:

```
[AS-PUBLISHED (getObjectSchema)]                       0 diagnostic(s)
[NEGATIVE CONTROL (the page's old 'getMetadata')]      2 diagnostic(s)
    TS2344: Type '... | "getMetadata"' does not satisfy the constraint 'keyof DataSource[any]'.
    TS2741: Property 'getObjectSchema' is missing in type 'M' but required in type 'DataSource[any]'.
```

So the `Pick` is not silently `any`: the exact spelling the page used to teach is the exact spelling the compiler now rejects.

### The elision decision, under the four axes

The `// ... implement other methods` elision in the example fence — the same shape #5174's batch 37 repaired in the root README with an ambient `declare class ... implements DataSource`. The choice here was between that ambient-class treatment, a hand-written members table, and a **fully written example annotated `: DataSource`**. Taken: the annotated full example.

- **实际业务需求** — measured, not assumed: the consuming prop is `ObjectViewProps.dataSource: DataSource`, required. The reader's real task is producing a value that satisfies it, and the thing that fails them is a missing member, not an unclear shape. A `declare class` teaches the shape but hands back nothing runnable; the annotated literal is copy-paste-able and still complete. The members-table option was rejected on this axis too, but for a sharper reason: a hand-copied signature table is exactly the drift hazard this gate's own header records against itself (objectui#7448 — "a pointer to the list now rather than a copy of its length"). Signatures are inferred from the contract in the new example, so there is no second copy to drift.
- **项目长远合理性** — contract-first. The page had become a *second* declaration of a contract `@object-ui/types` already owns; the repair deletes the second contract rather than syncing it. Nothing on the page restates a signature any more, so there is no maintenance coupling left to forget.
- **防 AI 写代码犯错** — this is the axis that decided it. The elision was a hole an agent fills by guessing; a guessed member set is exactly the batch-error shape the axis names. The annotation converts the hole into a **loud compile-time refusal**: an incomplete adapter stops the block compiling, and `check:doc-snippets` fails naming this file. Contract tightening over consumer tolerance, and the declaration is enforced rather than merely written — no `??`-style fallback anywhere near it. The ambient `declare class` scores nearly as well here, and loses only on the business-need axis above.
- **创业阶段不扩散需求** — nothing is exported, no capability surface grows. `MinimalDataSource` is a local alias inside a documentation block, not a published type, and route 乙 (a new exported "minimal adapter" contract) is explicitly declined. No staged window, no dual spelling: the wrong interface is deleted in this PR rather than deprecated beside the right one.

No axis conflicts here — all four point the same way, so nothing is escalated.

## Card #8161 — the re-derived zero, with a live control

**The card's own control is dead, and the PM's finding is confirmed.** The card offered: *"`git grep -n 'use client' origin/main -- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is empty; control: the same grep over `packages/app-shell/src` is non-empty."* Re-run, with exit codes captured by redirect (never through a pipe — `| head` closes the read end and hands the producer a SIGPIPE-flavoured 0):

```
[CARD-ZERO   docs/ARCHITECTURE.md]     exit=1  lines=0
[DEAD-CONTROL packages/app-shell/src]  exit=1  lines=0     <-- fires identically to the subject
[LIVE-CONTROL apps/site/app]           exit=0  lines=8
[REPO-WIDE]                            exit=0  lines=75
```

`packages/app-shell/src` returns the **same** reading as the subject, so it could never distinguish "the grep works and the page has none" from "the grep is broken". As written, the card's zero was unbacked.

**Live control**, same grep invocation, a population that actually fires: `apps/site/app` — 8 files, including `apps/site/app/components/InteractiveDemo.tsx` and `apps/site/app/playground/page.tsx`; 75 files repo-wide. Against that control the zero on `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (exit=1, 0 lines) **is** a reading. The card's conclusion survives; only its control had to be replaced.

The dead control also turned out to be a *fact worth teaching* rather than merely a broken instrument. `'use client'` occurs zero times not just in `packages/app-shell/src` but in the **built output** of every package these fences import:

```
packages/app-shell/dist    -> 0 file(s)
packages/providers/dist    -> 0 file(s)
packages/plugin-view/dist  -> 0 file(s)
packages/react/dist        -> 0 file(s)
```

That is precisely *why* the consumer's `app/` files have to carry the directive, and it is now the substance of the explanatory sentence.

### The teaching choice: which file carries the directive

Triage left this open — layout, page, or both. Taken: **both**, with one sentence of prose above the pair rather than a comment inside each fence.

Under the same four axes, briefly: the **business-need** axis settles it on measurement, not taste. Each fence needs it for an independent reason — `app/[object]/page.tsx` calls the `useDataSource()` hook, and `app/layout.tsx` renders `ThemeProvider` / `AppShell`, whose React context cannot be created on the server. Marking only the page would leave the layout broken; marking only the layout does not make a child module a client module (the directive is per-module, not inherited). On the **AI-error** axis, a reader or agent copying one fence in isolation gets a correct file either way, which a single shared directive would not deliver. On **long-term sanity**, the prose states the underlying rule — every module under `app/` is a server component by default — so the reader can generalise instead of pattern-matching a line. **Scope** stays flat: prose plus one line per fence, no new page section.

`Example 3: Embedded Widget` deliberately does **not** get the directive: its fence declares no `app/` file path and the directive is App-Router-specific. The explanatory sentence is scoped to Example 2 for the same reason.

⚠️ **The gate cannot check this half, and does not claim to.** Each fence compiles as an isolated module, so `'use client'` is just a string-expression statement to the TypeScript program — nothing in `check:doc-snippets` (or any other gate) validates a React Server Components boundary. #8161's evidence is the grep re-derivation above plus the `dist` census, and that is the whole of it. Do not read this PR's green gates as coverage of the directive.

## Controls

**Positive control for the doc gate, on the committed tree**, with trap-based restore. Mutation proven on disk *before* any gate result was read; restore proven by blob hash and an empty `git diff HEAD`:

```
HEAD blob:      304a349efe11c085e8ef7ff54f691ec50b0828be
ON-DISK MUTATION PROOF: old-anchor before=1 after=0 ; injected-text count=1
mutated blob:   9d0e755c906e824d3b334b488120862bcf739942   (differs from HEAD blob)

=== GATE ON MUTATED TREE ===   MUTATED_EXIT=1
  [semantic]  docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:287:3   TS2344: '"getObjectSchemaX"' is not assignable to type 'keyof DataSource[any]'. Did you mean '"getObjectSchema"'?
  [semantic]  docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:295:14  TS2741: Property 'getObjectSchema' is missing in type 'MinimalDataSource' but required in type 'DataSource[any]'.
  Semantic phase: 632 of 632 block(s) judged, 1 failed.

restored blob:  304a349efe11c085e8ef7ff54f691ec50b0828be   (equals HEAD blob)
git diff HEAD lines after restore: 0
still-injected count after restore: 0

=== GATE ON RESTORED TREE ===  RESTORED_EXIT=0
  Semantic phase: 632 of 632 block(s) judged, 0 failed.
```

Breaking one member name in the **repaired** fence makes the gate go red **naming `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**; unmodified, it is green in the same run. The repaired fence is genuinely load-bearing.

**Harness controls** (printed by the gate itself on every run): `resolution` lands on `packages/types/dist/index.d.ts` (a built artifact, not source); `sentinel` produces TS2305; `positive` produces 0; `undeclared` and `root-declared` each produce TS2307.

### Gate totals — re-measured, and one number differs from the dispatch

| | dispatch said | measured, both before and after this change |
|---|---|---|
| documents / covered / ungated | 229 / 229 / 0 | **229 / 229 / 0** — unchanged |
| whole-repo semantic phase | 631 of 631 | **632 of 632, 0 failed** |

The semantic total is **632**, not the 631 the dispatch carried from the last landing — one block joined the corpus between that landing and today's `origin/main` (`411a132c0`). It reads 632 identically *before* and *after* this change, so the difference is not this PR's: the corpus moved under the dispatch note, not under this diff. No regression either way; this PR replaces two fences with two fences, so the block count is flat at 790 (632 to compile, 158 declared fragments).

## Gates — every exit code by redirect, never through a pipe

| gate | exit | note |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm check:doc-snippets` | **0** | 229/229/0 documents; 632 of 632 blocks judged, 0 failed |
| `pnpm check:doc-examples` | **0** | 124 blocks, 90 ledger-declared failures unchanged |
| `pnpm check:doc-fences` | **0** | 227 documents |
| `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` | **0** | valid across 17 scan roots |
| `pnpm check:doc-types` | **0** | 188 files, 890 `type` literals, all registered |
| `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/` | **0** | 120 files, 3575 tests passed |
| `pnpm lint:root` | **0** | 32 warnings, **0 errors**, all pre-existing; note this script passes `--ignore-pattern 'docs/**'`, so it does not read the changed file |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | **0** | 6638 tracked text files |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | **0** | no changeset owed — 1 file changed, 0 of it published source of a released package |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | **0** | **NOT GOVERNED** — none of the 5 governed surfaces matched |

The build closure the doc gate prescribes (`--build-filter`, 34 packages) was built first: `turbo run build --concurrency=2`, 35/35 tasks successful. Without it the gate exits 2 ("could not run"), which is not a verdict about any document.

An independent control-byte self-scan over the changed file, beyond the gate: `grep -naP '[\x00-\x08\x0b\x0c\x0e-\x1f\x7f]' docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` exits 1 with no output.

---

Left **draft** deliberately. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` is *not* a governed surface (the guard says so above), so this is an ordinary PR on the normal route — the draft state is a seat convention here, not a governed-surface hold.
